newsitem.title: USA: Barron's poll sees Dow high at 6447.63 in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Barron's poll sees Dow high at 6447.63 in 1997.

text.p: Money managers see the Dow Jones Industrial Average at a high of 6,447.63 in 1997, as 41.2 percent held a neutral investment outlook through the middle of 1997 and 38.2 percent through the end of 1997, a Barron's survey said.

Of the 212 money managers surveyed, 35.5 percent said they were bullish in their investment outlook through mid-year 1997 and 31 percent hold that view through the end of 1997, reported Barron's, a financial weekly.
A July Barron's survey found money managers to be more bearish in their outlook.
Slightly more than 23 percent were bearish on the outlook through the middle of the year and 30.5 hold that view through the end of the year, the latest survey said.
Barron's conducted its "Big Money Poll" in late October. The Dow was at approximately 6000, the S&P 500 at 702 and the Nasdaq at approximately 1250 when the survey was taken.

In the meantime, stock markets have rallied after President Clinton was re-elected and Republicans retained control of Congress. On Friday, the Dow closed at 6219.82, the S&P 500 at 730.82 and the Nasdaq composite at 1257.51.
On average, the money managers surveyed see the Dow at a low of 5,391 in 1997.
Barron's said the bullish sentiment increased from July, when 28 percent of managers surveyed described themselves as bullish. In the July survey, 32 percent expected the market to decline.
Investment managers rated technology, energy, financial, oil services, consumer staples and pharmaceutical companies as the most most popular investments, the survey said.
Tobacco, consumer cyclicals, technology, electric utilities, airlines, basic materials and the automotive sectors were described as the least popular investments, the survey said.
